chapter: Cab Calloway, Harlem and New York musicians
title: Louis Steele, the drummer who swung with his whole body
summary: Danny describes the neat former-waiter drummer Steele and his full-body brushwork.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Well, I just wanted to bring that in. Then I want to go back to New York, where you are. Because I want to ask you about a friend of yours, a guy I used to see who was a very neat man, named Steele(?).
Steele(?) was a drummer... He'd been a waiter until he finally started playing drums. And he was from Florida, and he had migrated to New York as a kid. He was...

Yeah. Well, he was sharp. And he was into things. He wanted to be into things. He had a very quick temper. And he wanted to play drums, and he played drums; you know, New York swing drumming, they called it, in which you throw your whole body into motion when you play with
And if you were setting a tempo, you had to... Because once he gets that little sassy swish he did on his seat, you had to say somewhat with him.
Or whatever he did, he did it in the whole body. You'd almost throw your whole body into it.
I would give about a dollar for a videotape of this with you.
